A Misunderstanding

一场误会 · 184 词 · 3 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1In general, speech is our major way of communicating, but body language and facial expressions have a similar function. For example, yawning can show a lack of interest, while turning your back on someone or shaking a fist can show anger. But interpretations of gestures can be subjective and can vary from one culture to another. Thus, misunderstandings happen now and then at such cultural crossroads.

2Once, representing the Adults’ Education Association, I went to the airport to meet a high-ranking official from Colombia and take him to his dormitory and then to the canteen. When the flight arrived, I saw a man looking around curiously. So I approached to greet him. He suddenly dashed over to hug me and kissed me on both cheeks. As a young girl, I felt truly embarrassed and put up my hands to defend myself. His forced smile told me he felt that he had lost face.

3Later, I received a cassette from him, in which he recorded his apology. On hearing that Colombians were more likely to greet people with a kiss, I soon felt at ease.

一场误会

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1一般来说，口头语言是主要的交流方式，肢体语言和面部表情也能传递信息。比如，打哈欠可能表示不感兴趣，转过身背对别人或挥拳可能表示生气。不过，这些动作到底是什么意思，要看不同文化中的人怎样理解。如今各地文化常常交汇，误会也就时有发生。

2有一次，我代表成人教育协会到机场接一位哥伦比亚的高级官员，打算先送他去宿舍，再带他去食堂。飞机到了以后，我看见一个男子好奇地四处张望，便走过去打招呼。他突然冲过来拥抱我，还在我两边脸颊上各亲了一下。那时我还是个年轻女孩，顿时觉得很尴尬，下意识抬手挡了一下。他勉强挤出笑容，我看得出来他觉得很没面子。

3后来，他寄来一盘录音带，在里面向我道了歉。听他解释哥伦比亚人更常用亲吻来打招呼，我很快就不再紧张了。
